instructions:
You are labelling supersession decisions for an engineering-memory system. Each row is a pair of candidate memories extracted from two different public discussion threads of the same open-source project (contributor names are pseudonyms). `memory_a` is the EARLIER memory and `memory_b` the LATER one; each has `item` (a preference, convention or stance, rendered as "<category> preference (<polarity>, strength s): <key> about <entity>") and `quote` (its cited evidence).

Decide `label`: does memory_b SUPERSEDE memory_a, so that a memory system should treat memory_a as no longer current once memory_b is stored?

yes when memory_b is about the same subject as memory_a and replaces it: it reverses or contradicts it, narrows or changes it so that memory_a as stated is now wrong or out of date, or records a later decision that settles what memory_a left open in a different way.

no when they are about different subjects, when both can be true at once (compatible, complementary or merely related), when memory_b restates or duplicates memory_a without changing it, or when memory_b is only a more specific instance that leaves memory_a intact.

Strength numbers are not part of the judgement. Judge only from the row.
